reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Confusing with the original Fisher scale.
name: Modified Fisher Scale

version.label: Modified Fisher (Frontera et al. 2006)
version.detail: Grade 0–4 from cisternal clot thickness and IVH. Distinct from the original Fisher scale.

purpose: CT grading of SAH blood burden associated with symptomatic vasospasm.
intendedPopulation: Patients with aneurysmal SAH, on the admission CT.

options.label: Thin (focal or diffuse)
options.detail: Not completely filling a cistern or fissure.

options.label: Thick
options.detail: Completely filling at least one cistern or fissure.

resultStates.label: Not defined
resultStates.summary: The modified Fisher scale does not define IVH without subarachnoid blood.

resultStates.label: Grade 0
resultStates.summary: No SAH or IVH on this CT at this assessment.

resultStates.label: Grade 1
resultStates.summary: Thin SAH, no IVH (reference group with grade 0).

resultStates.label: Grade 2
resultStates.summary: Thin SAH with IVH. Crude odds ratio for symptomatic vasospasm 1.6 versus grades 0–1.

resultStates.label: Grade 3
resultStates.summary: Thick SAH, no IVH. Crude odds ratio 1.6 versus grades 0–1.

resultStates.label: Grade 4
resultStates.summary: Thick SAH with IVH. Crude odds ratio 2.2 versus grades 0–1.
resultStates.detail: Group-level association; correlate with clinical grade and monitoring according to local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: A CT grade with a more consistent relationship to vasospasm than the original Fisher scale.

clinicalInsights.text: Odds ratios come from the derivation cohort (placebo arms of tirilazad trials).

limitations.text: The original study did not define a measurement threshold for thick versus thin blood.

limitations: IVH is binary regardless of volume.

guideSections.what: A 0–4 CT grade from cisternal blood thickness and IVH.
guideSections.howToPerform: 0 none; 1 thin, no IVH; 2 thin + IVH; 3 thick, no IVH; 4 thick + IVH.

sources.citation: Frontera JA, Claassen J, Schmidt JM, et al. Prediction of symptomatic vasospasm after subarachnoid hemorrhage: the modified Fisher scale. Neurosurgery. 2006;59(1):21-27.
